content.text:
I read the brief line by line against the 8-K Exhibit 99.1 and checked every figure, period and GAAP/non-GAAP basis.

**Summary:** The brief is numerically clean — I found no wrong figures, periods or basis swaps. Its weaknesses are omissions: the reiterated full-year 2026 adjusted EPS range of $2.25–$2.35 never appears, the ~$24 billion 2026–2028 repurchase envelope is replaced by the broader $45 billion+ return plan, and the prior-year free cash flow ($4.4B) and Legacy dollar revenue ($1,632M) comparatives are dropped even though the percentage/current-period figures given are right.

facts.evidence: Revenues totaled $31.6 billion, representing a 2.3% increase from the year-ago quarter.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, while adjusted EPS was $0.65; both figures reflect increases versus the year-ago quarter of $0.62 and $0.54, respectively.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, while adjusted EPS was $0.65; both figures reflect increases versus the year-ago quarter of $0.62 and $0.54, respectively.
Advanced Connectivity service revenues grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion, driving a 20.3% increase in operating income and an 8.0% rise in EBITDA*.
Adjusted EBITDA was $12.3 billion, up 5.2% year over year, supported by cash from operating activities of $10.8 billion and free cash flow of $4.7 billion.
The Company plans to return $45 billion+ to shareholders during 2026-2028 through dividends and share repurchases, including approximately $10 billion of share repurchases in 2026.
supported by cash from operating activities of $10.8 billion and free cash flow of $4.7 billion
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year as the Company continues to decommission its copper-based network, resulting in a 45.5% decrease in operating income.
The Company added over 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers, comprising 646,000 total internet net adds (367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless) and 432,000 postpaid phone net adds.

claims.claim: Revenues totaled $31.6 billion in the second quarter.
Revenues increased 2.3% from the year-ago quarter.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66.
Adjusted EPS was $0.65.
Year-ago diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.62 and year-ago adjusted EPS was $0.54, so both measures increased year over year.
Operating income was $7.0 billion.
Adjusted operating income was $7.5 billion, compared with $6.5 billion in the prior-year period.
Adjusted EBITDA was $12.3 billion, up 5.2% year over year.
Cash from operating activities was $10.8 billion.
Free cash flow was $4.7 billion.
Advanced Connectivity service revenues grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion.
That service revenue growth drove a 20.3% increase in Advanced Connectivity operating income and an 8.0% rise in Advanced Connectivity EBITDA.
The Company added over 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers.
Total internet net adds were 646,000, including 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless.
Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year.
The Legacy revenue decline occurs as the Company continues to decommission its copper-based network.
Legacy segment operating income decreased 45.5% year over year.
Latin America segment revenues increased 16.1% year over year.
Latin America growth was primarily driven by favorable foreign exchange rates and postpaid wireless subscriber growth.
AT&T maintains its outlook for improved growth in adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS and higher free cash flow through 2028.
Service revenue growth is projected in the low-single-digit range annually.
The Company plans to return $45 billion+ to shareholders during 2026-2028 through dividends and share repurchases.
That return plan includes approximately $10 billion of share repurchases in 2026.
Advanced Connectivity EBITDA is expected to grow in the mid-to-high-single-digit range annually.
Legacy EBITDA is expected to turn negative after 2027, until direct costs associated with the copper-based network are substantially eliminated.
Total debt was $144.0 billion at the end of the second quarter.
Net debt was $126.4 billion.
Capital investment totaled $6.1 billion for the quarter, compared with $5.1 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Capital investment reflects ongoing spending for strategic initiatives.
The Company returned $4.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter.
That included approximately $2.2 billion in common share repurchases under the 2024 authorization.
AT&T acquired Lumen's mass markets fiber business in the first quarter.
The acquired mass markets fiber business generated incremental customer costs that raised operating expenses.
The release ties the net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA target (2.5x range) to a period of approximately three years following the closing of the EchoStar transaction.
An asset abandonment charge associated with the reprioritization of the Company's spectrum strategy increased operating expenses.
